name: Lechfall
kurzbeschreibung: The spectacular Lechfall on the Tyrolean-Bavarian border: 12 m stepped weir cascading into the Lechschlucht, historic Maxsteg from 1895, and Lechweg finale.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Lechfall is an impressive natural and industrial heritage monument on the southern edge of Füssen, directly on the state border between the Tyrolean Außerfern (district of Reutte) and Bavaria. At this striking narrow gorge, the Lech—the last great wild river of the Northern Alps—roars across its entire breadth over a twelve-metre-high, five-stepped weir into the deep, canyon-like Lechschlucht. As a designated protected geotop and scenic highlight, the waterfall marks the ceremonial finale of the 125-kilometre European long-distance trail Lechweg.

Geology, Maxsteg & History

The formation of the rock gorge dates back to the Würm glaciation around 12,000 years ago: as the Lech glacier retreated, a colossal glacial meltwater lake formed in the valley basin. When overflowing, the rushing waters carved through the hard Wetterstein limestone ridge, cutting an exceptionally narrow, ravine-like canyon into the solid rock. To harness hydropower for local mills and prevent hazardous logjams during log driving, the natural cascade was fortified during the 18th century with a meticulously constructed five-stepped weir. The premier vantage point is the Maxsteg: this daring iron pedestrian bridge was built in 1895 and spans directly above the churning, frothing torrent from one rock face to the other. It is named in honour of King Maximilian II. von Bayern, whose stone bust is enshrined in an alcove high above the gorge. Adjacent to the bust, the Magnustritt rock indentation commemorates the legend of Saint Magnus, who is said to have leaped across the chasm in a single bound while escaping pursuers.

Visit & Getting There

The Lechfall, the Maxsteg, and the scenic viewing platforms are freely and openly accessible free of charge 24 hours a day year-round (in winter, severe frost creates mesmerizing ice cascades). Arrival by car: from Tyrol via the Fernpassstraße B179 through Reutte and Pflach onto the B17 or Tiroler Straße straight to the Füssen border crossing; a pay-and-display parking area is situated directly on Tiroler Straße just above the falls. By public transport: take ÖBB trains to Bahnhof Reutte in Tirol or DB trains to Bahnhof Füssen; from Füssen it is a scenic 15-minute walk along the König-Ludwig-Promenadenweg to the falls, while regional buses link Reutte to the border.

Tips

The viewing platform adjacent to the roadside is step-free and barrier-free for wheelchair users and pushchairs; the historic Maxsteg is accessed via just a few steps. Visit the waterfall especially after heavy rainfalls or during the alpine snowmelt in early summer, when torrential waters thunder over the weir with deafening power. A visit to Lechfall pairs wonderfully with the nearby Walderlebniszentrum Ziegelwies with its spectacular treetop walkway.
